text:
Ana_Sales: heads up — rolling out a small change to how we version rate cards starting next week. new policy: semantic-like versioning + explicit branch tag for POCs/commits. doc here: https://redwood.internal/ratecard/versioning (TL;DR below)
Sarah_Ops: thanks Ana. quick Q — does this affect quoting for live commits this month?
Ana_Sales: no immediate price changes. main impact is metadata: every quote must include ratecard_version + branch tag. for existing committed deals we’ll auto-map to the active branch unless sales requests grandfathering.
MikeG: how does this look in the quote payload? can we add an example snippet for quoting tool?
Ana_Sales: yes — example we plan to standardize:
```
ratecard_version: "v2026.03.1"
ratecard_branch: "stable"   # or "poc/healthtech-2026"
commit_tier: "S1"
```
Ravi_Finance: if sales tags a deal with a poc branch, does that affect revenue recognition or invoicing? need clarity for finance systems.
Ana_Sales: good call. finance: tagging is purely informational for now. invoicing uses SKU IDs as usual. if a branch includes temporary discounts we’ll require a deal-desk approval id in the quote metadata.
Deal-Desk: we’ll need a short process for approvals. propose a Slack reaction workflow: :white_check_mark: + PR number -> we attach approval id. if discount >10% require deal desk review.
Sarah_Ops: also flagging: our billing export needs a new column for ratecard_branch. engineering, can you add that to downstream CSVs? @release-bot can we track this as a minor release?
release-bot: release created: infra/ratecard-metadata -> v0.3. target deploy window: Thu 03:00-05:00 UTC. changelog: add ratecard_branch field to exports, validation for quote metadata.
MikeG: ops — if a customer signs under a poc branch and later wants to migrate to stable pricing, what’s the formal migration path?
Ana_Sales: plan: 1) optional migration credit window (30 days) if commit still within initial term, 2) deal-desk approval for any price parity exceptions, 3) update quote + re-issue invoice if needed. will draft runbook.
Ravi_Finance: please include examples of journal entries in the runbook. helps us automate reconciliation.
Deal-Desk: noted. we'll assemble an approvals checklist: fields required, max discount thresholds, who signs off. want a simple checkbox form.
Sarah_Ops: one more thing — can we add a validation that prevents creating quote with nonexistent ratecard_version? prevents accidental typos.
Ana_Sales: yes that’s in the plan. server-side validation + helpful error message in quote API.
MikeG: thanks — can you ping engineering & support channels when the migration doc + form live? I have a few deals that will need special handling this week.
Ana_Sales: will do. pinging product & eng shortly. for now, if you have urgent POC quotes that need special terms, DM me or drop @Deal-Desk here with the thread id.
Deal-Desk: please include the customer name, sku lines, and proposed discount %. we'll triage.
Sarah_Ops: cool — thanks all. small ask: can we backfill ratecard_branch for quotes created this month so exports stay consistent?
Ravi_Finance: backfill ok if there is a clear rule. prefer branch='stable' by default unless flagged.
Ana_Sales: agreed. default stable backfill. I'll follow up with the backfill window and timeline.
